claims.text: Header block: DoD Directive 5205.07, 'Special Access Program Policy'; effective September 12, 2024; releasability 'Cleared for public release'; 'Reissues and Cancels: DoD Directive 5205.07, July 1, 2010, as amended'; approved by Kathleen H. Hicks, Deputy Secretary of Defense.

Policy para 1.2 verbatim in part: 'The DoD will establish and apply SAP security protection to classified national security information in accordance with E.O. 13526; Part 2001 of Title 32, Code of Federal Regulations; DoD Instruction (DoDI) 5200.01; and DoD Manual 5200.01.' Also: 'The DoD will have SAP oversight authorities (OAs) to oversee SAPs for which the OA has responsibility.'

The directive places the Director, DoD SAPCO 'under the authority, direction, and control of the Deputy Secretary of Defense' and requires the position be filled by 'a general officer, flag officer, or Senior Executive Service member or equivalent appointed to oversee day-to-day management of the SAP Enterprise.' The Deputy Secretary of Defense chairs the SAPOC.

CONTRACTOR SPEECH RESTRICTION. The directive states that no DoD contractor entity 'will provide SAP material to any members of Congress or their staff without Director, DoD SAPCO approval.' The Director, DoD SAPCO is designated the primary point of contact for congressional SAP matters and 'Maintains records of DoD SAP information provided to Congress.'

NEGATIVE FINDING WITH CONSEQUENCE. A full-text pass of the 12 September 2024 directive found no occurrence of the terms 'carve-out', 'waived', 'unacknowledged', 'notification', or '10 U.S.C. 119'. The 2024 reissuance moved every operative concealment mechanism out of the public-release Directive and into the companion Instruction, DoDI 5205.11 — which remains public but is the document one must know to ask for.

DoDD 5205.07 (12 September 2024) cancels DoD Directive 5205.07 of 1 July 2010, as amended, and incorporates the Deputy Secretary of Defense Memorandum, 'Implementation Guidance for DoD Special Access Program Enterprise Reform', 11 July 2023.

DoDD 5205.07 (2024) defines 'Joint Force Integration SAP' as 'A SAP intended for greater integration and sharing across the Joint Force and the broader SAP community' and 'Strategic Enabler SAP' as 'A SAP protecting capabilities or information that enable strategic competition and warrant more limited and restrictive sharing.'
DoDD 5205.07 (2024) section 3.1.d: 'Establishment of new SAP umbrellas and compartments will be by exception. Establishment ... requires Secretary of Defense or Deputy Secretary of Defense approval.'
DoDD 5205.07 (2024) describes the SAPOC as 'the senior governing body of the DoD SAP Enterprise for governance, management, and oversight of DoD SAPs', chaired by the Deputy Secretary of Defense.

claims.text: DoDD 5205.07 (2024) makes the Director, DoD SAPCO the 'primary point of contact for SAP matters with ... the Legislative Branch' and requires that 'All personnel accessed to DoD SAPs will notify the Director, DoD SAPCO ... when briefing or providing DoD SAP material to any member of Congress.'

claims.text: The definitions section of DoDD 5205.07 (2024) does not contain definitions for 'acknowledged SAP', 'unacknowledged SAP', 'waived SAP' or 'carve-out', all of which appeared in the 2010 version it cancels.

32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) still conditions relief of DCSA oversight on a carve-out approved 'in accordance with DoDD 5205.07', but the current DoDD 5205.07 no longer defines carve-out - leaving a regulation that points at a directive that no longer contains the term. Reasoning: comparison of the operative CFR text with the 2024 reissue's glossary.

connections.note: Same policy instrument, two issuances, and the programmatic relation is what CHANGED between them - which is not the same fact as the supersession recorded on the temporal edge. The 2010 directive's glossary defines 'carve-out' as 'a provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense that relieves DSS of its National Industrial Security Program oversight', and its Enclosure 2 para 5 restates the statutory waiver in policy. A full-text pass of the 12 September 2024 reissue finds no occurrence of 'carve-out', 'waived' or 'unacknowledged' at all. The vocabulary the earlier directive defined is simply absent from the later one. Note what that does and does not establish: 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) still carries the carve-out in codified regulation, and still points at DoDD 5205.07 by name, so the mechanism did not end when the words left the directive.

desc: The current directive, effective 12 September 2024, cancels the 1 July 2010 version as amended and incorporates the Deputy Secretary of Defense memorandum 'Implementation Guidance for DoD Special Access Program Enterprise Reform' of 11 July 2023. Two changes matter for this board. First, the governance structure is retained and strengthened: the SAPOC remains 'the senior governing body of the DoD SAP Enterprise for governance, management, and oversight of DoD SAPs', chaired by the Deputy Secretary of Defense, with the Director of DoD SAPCO as Executive Secretary of the SAPOC and the SRG and Chair of the SSWG, reporting directly to the Deputy Secretary. Establishment of new SAP umbrellas and compartments is stated to be 'by exception' and requires Secretary or Deputy Secretary approval. Second, and much more significant, the 2024 directive replaces the acknowledged / unacknowledged / waived taxonomy with two new categories - 'Joint Force Integration SAP', defined as 'A SAP intended for greater integration and sharing across the Joint Force and the broader SAP community', and 'Strategic Enabler SAP', defined as 'A SAP protecting capabilities or information that enable strategic competition and warrant more limited and restrictive sharing'. The words acknowledged, unacknowledged, waived and carve-out do not appear in its definitions section. This does not repeal 10 U.S.C. 119(e), which continues to authorise the reporting waiver, and it does not repeal 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3), which continues to authorise the carve-out and still cites this very directive by number. The effect is that the two mechanisms most relevant to a concealed program survive in statute and in the Code of Federal Regulations while ceasing to be defined in the Department's own public charter - the terminology has been removed from the shop window without being removed from the shop. The directive also carries forward the congressional-contact reporting rule: 'All personnel accessed to DoD SAPs will notify the Director, DoD SAPCO ... when briefing or providing DoD SAP material to any member of Congress.'

timeline.text: The reissued DoD Directive 5205.07 cancels the 2010 version, incorporates the 11 July 2023 SAP Enterprise Reform guidance, and replaces the three-state taxonomy with 'Joint Force Integration SAP' and 'Strategic Enabler SAP'. Neither 10 U.S.C. 119(e) nor 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) is repealed; the mechanisms survive while the vocabulary is removed from the public charter.
